testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What happens if an engine runs without oil?

options.text: The vehicle will use less gas.
The engine can be destroyed quickly.
The Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) will not work properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine can be destroyed quickly.
questions.explanation: Engine oil is critical for protecting the engine. Without enough oil, an engine can be destroyed very quickly.

questions.question: A cargo van with a light load is usually:

options.text: The same height as when carrying a heavy load.
Taller than when carrying a heavy load.
Shorter than when carrying a heavy load.
Less stable than when carrying a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taller than when carrying a heavy load.
questions.explanation: A heavy load pushes a vehicle lower to the ground. A light load makes a vehicle sit higher. A vehicle that fits under an overpass when empty may not fit when fully loaded.

questions.question: What can affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?

options.text: Speed.
Sunshine.
Time of day.
Traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on how fast you are driving, how heavy your vehicle is, and how slippery the road surface is.

questions.question: When you see a construction worker near the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Slow down.
Stay out of all lanes.
Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Always reduce your speed when driving through work zones where workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: During a CDL vehicle inspection test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Replace a tire.
Remove the alternator belt.
Replace spark plugs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level.
questions.explanation: The CDL vehicle inspection test requires you to complete a full vehicle inspection, which includes checking the engine oil level.

questions.question: How can you avoid getting drowsy on a trip?

options.text: Get about four hours of sleep.
Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
Drive alone.
Schedule long trips at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan stopping points into your trip in advance.
questions.explanation: To stay alert on a long trip, get plenty of sleep beforehand, plan your route and stopping points ahead of time, drive with a passenger, and drive during hours when you are normally awake.

questions.question: Why should you frequently check your tires in your mirrors?

options.text: To watch for tire fires.
To see if the tires are rolling properly.
To check if the tread is deep enough.
To compare tire size to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for tire fires.
questions.explanation: Check your tires regularly in your mirrors to spot a tire fire if one starts. Tire fires can happen when tires are under-inflated, when dual tires touch, or when tires overheat.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Apply the parking brake.
Apply the air brakes.
Not apply any brake.
Disconnect the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow you to drive faster than normal.
Allow you to follow other vehicles more closely.
Allow you to drive less carefully.
Does not reduce your stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not reduce your stopping distance.
questions.explanation: ABS helps you maintain control when braking hard. However, it does not necessarily make your vehicle stop in a shorter distance.

questions.question: When inspecting the engine compartment, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Check the engine oil level.
Check the coolant level in the radiator.
Drain the brake fluid.
Check the windshield washer fluid level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drain the brake fluid.
questions.explanation: During an engine compartment inspection, you should check the oil level, coolant level, and windshield washer fluid level. You should not drain the brake fluid.

questions.question: What happens when a front axle is underloaded?

options.text: It helps with smooth steering.
It is good because front axles are usually weaker than other axles.
It should be avoided because it can cause steering problems.
It should be avoided because it improves fuel efficiency.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should be avoided because it can cause steering problems.
questions.explanation: An underloaded front axle can make it unsafe to steer your vehicle. Always distribute weight evenly when loading cargo.

questions.question: How can you become more visible to other drivers at dawn or dusk?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Honk your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Turn on your windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in snowy or rainy conditions, turn on your headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if you pull over on the side of the road?

options.text: Use only the taillights to alert other drivers.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Keep your lights off so you don't distract other drivers.
Place items from your vehicle on the road to warn drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: When you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers and use warning signals to alert other drivers.

questions.question: Which tire condition is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Tires that are different sizes
Front tires with 3/32 inch of tread
Tires made by different manufacturers

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread. Do not use tires of different sizes.

questions.question: A CMV driver with any detectable alcohol in their system (but below the legal limit) will receive:

options.text: A 2-hour out-of-service order.
A 10-hour out-of-service order.
A 24-hour out-of-service order.

questions.correctAnswerText: A 24-hour out-of-service order.
questions.explanation: If you have any detectable alcohol in your system while driving a CMV, even if your blood alcohol is below 0.04 percent, you will be put out-of-service for 24 hours. Never drive under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: When steering to avoid a crash, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one hand to steer.
Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
Don't check your mirrors for other lanes.
Speed up as you get closer to the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep both hands on the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Always keep both hands on the steering wheel when turning quickly to avoid a hazard. You need a firm grip to turn quickly.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is in a crash ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and confront the driver.
Stop safely away from the crash, wait for police, and describe the driver's behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely away from the crash, wait for police, and describe the driver's behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop a safe distance away, wait for police to arrive, and tell them about the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, when can you exit the vehicle?

options.text: You cannot stop and exit the vehicle.
You are discouraged from exiting the vehicle.
You can exit only if the vehicle is in reverse.
You can exit only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can exit only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.
questions.explanation: During the basic control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting to check the vehicle's position. You can check the position no more than twice, except during straight line backing where you can look only once.

questions.question: Why are roads most slippery when rain first starts?

options.text: Water mixes with oil and grease already on the road.
Roads are naturally slippery.
Gravel gets washed to the middle of the lane.
Tires are not designed for rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with oil and grease already on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are slipperiest when rain first starts. Fresh rainwater mixes with oil and grease on the road surface to create a slick layer. This mixture washes away as rain continues.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, what is important to do?

options.text: Put as little weight as possible on the axles.
Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
Don't worry about how the weight is distributed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the right amount of weight on the axles.
questions.explanation: When loading cargo, make sure each axle carries the right amount of weight. Too little or too much weight can cause steering problems, reduce traction, or damage the axles.

questions.question: What does the S-cam do when it turns inside a brake drum?

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and pushes the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: How long does it take for engine oil pressure to reach normal after the engine starts?

options.text: Within seconds.
Within five minutes.
Within three minutes.
After five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within seconds.
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within seconds after the engine starts. Do not drive if the oil pressure is too low.

questions.question: What should a CMV driver do when making a tight turn?

options.text: Drive as fast as a car driver would.
Focus on the road without worrying about speed.
Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn drivers behind by braking early and slowing gradually.
questions.explanation: Drivers behind you may not realize how slowly your CMV needs to turn. Brake early and slow down gradually to warn them in advance.

questions.question: What should you do if the previous driver left a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: Skip your pre-trip inspection and use the report instead.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Review the report.
Talk to the previous driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the report.
questions.explanation: Your first step should be to read any inspection report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: Can you use a tractor without ABS if the trailer has ABS?

options.text: No, both the tractor and trailer must have ABS.
Yes, but drive more slowly than usual.
No, you need a new tractor with ABS.
Yes, you can use them together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, you can use them together.
questions.explanation: Having anti-lock brakes on only the tractor or only the trailer still provides better control during braking.

questions.question: When checking your windshield before a trip, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: Look for cracks or damage on the windshield. Check that wiper arms have proper spring tension. Look for damage, stiff rubber, or loose attachment on the wiper blades.

questions.question: What should you do during the stop/start maneuver on the skills test?

options.text: Cut off other vehicles to get onto the shoulder.
Do not use turn signals.
Slam on the brakes to stop as quickly as possible.
Slow down smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down smoothly.
questions.explanation: During the on-road skills test, you will pull over and stop as if checking your vehicle. Check traffic, turn on your signal, slow down smoothly with even braking and gear changes, and come to a complete stop without coasting.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Trouble focusing, with frequent blinking
Yawning repeatedly or rubbing your eyes
Staying in your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Staying in your lane
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting a shoulder rumble strip, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: What happens after two violations for hand-held phone use while driving?

options.text: You must cancel your mobile phone service.
Your CDL will be disqualified.
You must drive 10 mph under the speed limit for a period of time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your CDL will be disqualified.
questions.explanation: Two convictions for violating state hand-held phone laws will result in CDL disqualification. Penalties become worse with more violations.

questions.question: How does texting while driving compare to talking on a cell phone while driving?

options.text: It is much safer.
It is just as safe.
It is more dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is more dangerous.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is more dangerous than talking on the phone. It distracts you mentally and physically.

questions.question: If you see taillights ahead while driving in fog, what should you know?

options.text: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
You can be sure the vehicle ahead is on the road.
It may be an optical illusion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide to where the road is. A vehicle's lights may be coming from a car that has pulled off the road.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps an engine work properly:

options.text: Only when it is cold outside.
To use less fuel.
In both cold and hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: In both cold and hot weather.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle needs enough water and antifreeze in the cooling system at all times. Despite its name, antifreeze helps the engine even in hot weather.

questions.question: During a vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: When a driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
When a driver checks their blind spots.
When a driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when you open your door, get out, and walk to the back of your vehicle to check where it is. During straight line backing, you can only look once. During other exercises, you can look twice.

questions.question: What usually happens to bridges in freezing weather?

options.text: They do not freeze.
They have heaters to prevent freezing.
They freeze before other road surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before the rest of the road. Drive carefully on bridges when the temperature is near freezing.

questions.question: What should you do with a burning tire?

options.text: Cool it with water.
Fan it with a blanket.
Cut it up with an axe.
Cover it with a tarp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cool it with water.
questions.explanation: Cool a burning tire with water. You may need a lot of water to properly cool the tire.

questions.question: Why should you drain air tanks regularly?

options.text: Because the air gets old and needs replacing.
Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
To change the pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because compressed air contains water that collects in the tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains moisture and compressor oil that build up in the tanks and can damage the brake system. Drain the tanks to remove these materials. If your tank has a manual drain valve, drain it at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Who is responsible for cargo loaded on a truck?

options.text: The person who loaded the truck.
The supervisor of the company.
The truck driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver.
questions.explanation: Even if someone else loaded the cargo, the driver is responsible for checking it and making sure it is secured properly.

questions.question: A vehicle stopped at a green light may show that the driver:

options.text: Is impaired.
Is colorblind.
Does not know traffic rules.
Is very patient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is impaired.
questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs of impairment. Drivers who have drunk alcohol, are tired, are using drugs, or are sick can be dangerous. One warning sign is stopping in wrong places, like at green lights.

questions.question: Which is a good rule when making a turn?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn so you don't confuse other drivers.
Signal early.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal early.
questions.explanation: Give your signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep the signal on during the entire turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: A liver can process about ____ per hour.

options.text: One alcoholic drink.
Two alcoholic drinks.
Three alcoholic drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: One alcoholic drink.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the higher your blood alcohol level becomes. Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate of about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should make sure the spring brakes turn on automatically when:

options.text: Air pressure falls below 45 psi.
Air pressure falls below 20 psi.
Driving downhill.
Driving uphill.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure falls below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, check that spring brakes turn on when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. You can test this by blocking the wheels and letting air out of the brake system. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake should pop out and spring brakes should activate.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people from spilled cargo
To protect the cargo from weather
To protect the cargo from animals

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect the cargo from animals
questions.explanation: You should cover cargo to protect people if cargo spills and to protect cargo from bad weather. Protecting cargo from animals is not a main reason to cover cargo.

questions.question: When you need to back up, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk the path first to look for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk the path first to look for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk along the path to check for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both side mirrors.

questions.question: Who can operate a vehicle that requires hazmat placards?

options.text: Any driver with a CDL
A driver with a hazardous materials endorsement
A driver with at least 10 years of commercial driving experience
Any person who thinks they can

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver with a hazardous materials endorsement
questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to operate a vehicle that transports hazardous materials.

questions.question: Air tanks usually hold enough compressed air for:

options.text: One stop before needing to be refilled.
Several stops before needing to be refilled.
A day's worth of braking.
An unlimited number of stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Several stops before needing to be refilled.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in a braking system hold enough compressed air for the brakes to work several times.

questions.question: If you think the road might be icy but you are not sure, what should you do?

options.text: Guess.
Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
Look at the road closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open your window and feel the side mirror for ice.
questions.explanation: If you think the road might be icy, open your window and feel the front of the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If ice has formed on these items, the road is likely icy.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, what should a driver do?

options.text: Always set the parking brake.
Only set the parking brake if parked on a slope.
Let air out of the tires by 10 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always set the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: While moving.
When the trailers are straight.
When you are standing next to the vehicle.
By an assistant.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the trailers are straight.
questions.explanation: Check mirrors before starting a trip. For vehicles with trailers, you can only check mirror adjustment accurately when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: In very hot weather, why should you check tires regularly?

options.text: They may melt.
Air pressure may increase with temperature.
Tread wears down faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase with temperature.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Pay special attention to tire pressure and mounting when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: What is a problem with cargo that has a high center of gravity?

options.text: It can make a vehicle likely to tip over.
It is encouraged in bad weather.
It is required on some roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make a vehicle likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip over. Keep the weight of cargo as low as possible.
